Title: Quartz-style Nth Day of Week cron expressions can overflow to other month
Body:
## The issue

We are experiencing a weird issue with Cron Expressions. We are using the `@Scheduled` annotation to run scheduled jobs every monday.

We have a use case where we want to run a schedule differently if it is the first Monday of the month, which is why we split our schedules up into 2 CRON expressions, using the "day of week" notation ([documented here](<URL>


1. `0 0 8 ? * MON#1` - run every first Monday of the month
2.  `0 0 8 ? * MON#2,MON#3,MON#4,MON#5` - run on all other Mondays of the month

This worked fine until we observed weird behavior today on Monday the 3rd February 2025. The second CRON expression fired even though it should not fire on the first Monday of a month.

I run a test for the next 10000 invocations and these are the 10 dates that this unexpected overlap will happen next:

```The code snippet is a list of 12 `OffsetDateTime` objects in Java, each representing a date and time in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmZ`. All times are set to 08:00Z (UTC). The dates span from February 3, 2025, to February 4, 2047.```

## Conclusion

It seems as if the _day of week_ expression (e.g. `MON#5`) overflows **only** from January to February in the years where January has less than 5 Mondays. (This is why 31.1.2028 is not up there for example).


## Reproduction
This can be reproduced with spring-context-6.2.2 with following test case:

 ```This Java test case ensures that two cron expressions do not overlap within a specified number of invocations. It uses the `CronExpression` class from Spring to parse and schedule cron expressions, then checks for overlapping times between the two schedules.```

Title: UWP target (e.g. x86_64-uwp-windows-msvc) is broken
Body:
I tried to compile x86_64-uwp-windows-msvc on nightly rust using `-Z build-std` . I used `staticlib` as target type. Then I tried to link the successfully created .lib file into my exe - outside of rust ecosystem. The linker failed with this error:

```The log indicates an unresolved external symbol error for `__imp_NtOpenFile` when referencing it in the `_ZN3std3sys3pal7windows2fs14remove_dir_all12nt_open_file17h43bb929b19188a87E` function.```

My successful cargo command which created my staticlib which is unusable in UWP is:

```This command compiles a Rust library package named `pkg_name` using Cargo for the x86_64 UWP Windows MSVC target, including only the `std` and `panic_abort` libraries, and disables default linker libraries.```

The issue is due to rust's std lib using NtOpenFile function which is not available for UWP applications. This regression was introduced in <URL>

The usage of the function is not guarded by the `#[cfg(target_vendor = "uwp")]` feature here: <URL>

The way I understand it, all uwp targets are unusable since the above mentioned commit around September 2024 because the rust's std library uses function not allowed for uwp applications.

Title: `SegmentCommand.create` does not properly create a segment command with a non-zero number of sections
Body:
**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of the bug.

**To Reproduce**
Use the `SegmentCommand.create` method and pass a non-zero value to the `numSections` argument. The resulting bytes have a `cmdsize` parameter that does not account for the section definitions.

**Expected behavior**
The resulting bytes have a `cmdsize` parameter that *does* account for the section definitions.

**Additional context**
As far as I know, each section definition is of a guaranteed size, so it should be trivial to multiply that size by the number of sections and add it to the total size. The sections may not be included in the returned bytes, but at least the `cmdsize` parameter will be more accurate. The function could include null bytes of the correct size, if need be. At worst, it can throw if a non-zero value is passed to the `numSections` argument.

I understand this is a new-ish method, but is quite helpful for some work that I am doing. I am, however, having to manually re-do the `cmdsize` parameter afterwards and would prefer to not have to do that.

Title: CoercePointee doesn't support trait bounds on the smart pointer
Body:
I tried this code:

```The code snippet defines a custom Arc-like smart pointer `MyArc` for types that implement `MyTrait`. It uses Rust's `CoercePointee` and `arbitrary_self_types` features to create a transparent wrapper around `std::sync::Arc`. The `MyArc` struct is designed to be used with types implementing `MyOtherTrait`, which in turn extends `MyTrait`. The `test` function demonstrates using `MyArc` with a trait object of `MyOtherTrait`.```

I expected to see this happen: It compiles.
Instead, this happened: 
```````````````````The code snippet indicates that the trait `MyOtherTrait` is not dynamically compatible because its `foo` method has a self parameter of type `MyArc<Self>`. For a trait to be dynamically dispatchable (`dyn` compatible), its self parameter must be either `self: Self` (for non-reference types) or `&self: &Self` (for reference types). The error suggests changing the `foo` method's self parameter to `&Self`.```
